turns.text: I'm terrified of plagiarism. How do I use sources in my essay without getting in trouble?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good that you're thinking about it. The key rule is, whenever you use someone else's words or ideas, you say where they came from.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Even if I put it in my own words?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes. Paraphrasing still needs a reference, because the idea is still theirs.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Use quotation marks around the exact words, and reference them too. Most universities have a style guide that shows the format.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm getting my dad a new phone and I want to pick the right one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hold your thoughts until I've described all the options.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One is a simple phone with big buttons and a large screen, made for people who aren't techy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Another is the same brand he's using now, just the newer version, so everything feels familiar.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or there's a cheap basic smartphone that mostly does calls, texts and photos.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's the full list. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sticking with the same brand is probably the smoothest choice, he won't have to relearn anything. The big button phone is great if his eyesight is a concern. The basic smartphone saves money but might feel slow.
